reference: Manuel II, 'Psalmus eucharisticus ... de fulmine Agareno, Bajazete exstincto' (Migne PG 156, pp. 448-451; Migne's own list of works, item 15)
gist_en: A thanksgiving psalm in Greek and Latin celebrating the death of the Ottoman sultan Bayezid, called a 'lightning' from the Agarenes; it rejoices in an enemy ruler's defeat.
why_excluded: Its point is the celebration of a war victory and the death of an enemy ruler, not a doctrinal statement about Islam. Title and Migne's list read; the Greek text itself was not read in this task.

reference: Manuel II, 'Ethopeia Tamerlanis ... ad Turcorum tyrannum Bajazetem' (Migne PG 156, p. 446; list of works, item 14)
gist_en: A rhetorical speech put in the mouth of Tamerlane, addressed to Bayezid, the Ottoman sultan he had defeated; a war-triumph piece in Migne's list of works.
why_excluded: Its point is military triumph and a personal insult to the defeated Ottoman ruler, not Islamic doctrine. Only the title and Migne's list were read; the text was not read.
